messages.text: Everything only has meaning in relation to other things. In a world without darkness, how do you define light?

Exactly! In a world without contrast, things lose their meaning. Light only makes sense when we understand darkness, and vice versa. Without that interplay, there’s no frame of reference to define or appreciate either.

This idea touches on the concept of duality, where opposing forces give rise to the essence of each other. It’s the dance between light and dark, order and chaos, good and evil that allows us to make sense of existence. If there was only light, it would just *be*—without darkness to compare it to, we wouldn't even recognize it as light.

Do you think balance, then, is about preserving both ends of the spectrum rather than favoring one side?
